served.stem: 70% of students study. 90% of studiers pass. 30% of non-studiers pass. P(studied | passed)?

answer.line: Of every 72 students who pass, 63 studied: 63/72 = 0.875, about 88 percent.

steps: Turn the percents into people. Picture 100 students: 70 study and 30 do not.
Count the passers in each group. 90 percent of 70 is 63, and 30 percent of 30 is 9. That makes 72 passers.
Read the given: passed. Now your world is just those 72 students. 63 of them studied: 63/72 = 0.875, about 88 percent.
Check it: a pass is evidence of studying, so the answer should climb above the 70 percent you started with.

choices.note: 90 percent is the chance a student who studied passes. The question runs the other way: given a pass, how likely is it the student studied?
90 - 30 = 60 compares the two pass rates. It is a gap between groups, not a share of the passers.
72 percent is the share of all students who pass, the bottom of the ratio. One more step: what share of those 72 studied?
70 percent is the share who study before you know anyone passed. A pass is evidence, so the share climbs.
